messages:
customer-ops: Hey team — after yesterday's maintenance we started seeing embedding vector length go from 1024 -> 1536 and our search index is failing. We pinned the model on our side to the name we always used. Need urgent help, customer-facing search is degraded :sos:
elllen-support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the model identifier you're calling and a minimal request/response? Also any request_id from the failing calls would help. :eyes:
customer-ops: Sure. We're calling POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings with body `{\n  \"model\": \"mosaicml/mpt-7b-embeddings\",\n  \"input\": [\"example query\"]\n}`
Response (trimmed): `{\n  \"data\": [{\"embedding\": [0.001, 0.002, ...], \"metadata\": {\"dimensions\": 1536}}],\n  \"request_id\": \"req_01G9XYZ123\"\n}`
We used to get length 1024 vectors. We pinned what we thought was the old model name in our config. Indexer error (FAISS): `ValueError: dimension mismatch (expected 1024, got 1536)`
mike-eng: Two quick hypotheses: 1) The model artifact actually changed vector_size between releases (sometimes upstream changes the embedding head) and your pinning by model name only matched a moving tag. 2) There's a fallback/canary routing on our side that routed traffic to a different model variant that returns different dims. Can you run `GET /v1/models?name=mosaicml/mpt-7b-embeddings` and paste the `vector_size` and `id` fields? Also paste the full request_id — I want runtime logs for that request_id. :face_with_monocle:
sam-runtime: Also double-check you aren't hitting batch padding that concatenates multiple embedding outputs (rare but we've seen marshalling bugs cause shape changes). Can you run a single-request with `batching: false` or `max_batch_size: 1` in your client and show the raw bytes? If you can share the request_id I'll pull server logs.
customer-ops: Running `GET /v1/models?name=mosaicml/mpt-7b-embeddings` returned:
```
[{"id":"mpt-7b-emb-v2.1","name":"mosaicml/mpt-7b-embeddings","vector_size":1536,"tag":"v2.1"},
 {"id":"mpt-7b-emb-v1.9","name":"mosaicml/mpt-7b-embeddings","vector_size":1024,"tag":"v1.9"}]
```
Request id: `req_01G9XYZ123`
Also ran a single request with `max_batch_size:1` — still returned 1536. Hope that helps.
ryan-sre: deploy-bot shows a canary->stable promotion last night for `mpt-7b-emb-v2.1` at 2024-11-02T22:14Z. Looks like the new variant has a larger embedding head. Pasting deploy-bot message: `deploy-bot: promoted mpt-7b-emb-v2.1 to stable (canary 2024-11-02 22:14) by release-engineering` :information_source:
mike-eng: That aligns — model artifact changed. Two remediation paths: A) Roll your index forward — re-embed docs with 1536 vectors and re-build FAISS. B) If you must keep 1024, we can route your workspace to `mpt-7b-emb-v1.9` explicitly (pin to the artifact id) or roll your customers back while you re-index. We can pin at the platform level for your org so you don't pick up the stable promotion. I can help with either.
elllen-support: For pinning on Redwood, there's a safe API: `POST /v1/organizations/{org_id}/pinned_models` with body `{ \"model_id\": \"mpt-7b-emb-v1.9\" }`. If you want to pin to the immutable artifact use the full id `mpt-7b-emb-v1.9` or the sha: `mpt-7b-emb@sha:abcdef`. If you'd like us to do the pin for you, give us the org id and confirm. :+1:
customer-ops: We need time to re-index (it's a 12M doc index). Can you pin us to v1.9 for now? Also, can you explain why our client-side pin didn't work? We set `model: \"mosaicml/mpt-7b-embeddings@v1.9\"` in our config.
sam-runtime: If you included just the lightweight tag `@v1.9` but the platform's resolution prefers stable alias routing, it might still resolve to the promoted artifact unless the API call uses the exact immutable model id or sha. There's a subtlety: the public model name can have multiple artifact ids — using the exact `id` from the `GET /v1/models` list or the sha avoids ambiguity. Also confirm there wasn't credential caching in your SDK that retained an earlier `model` field — but since your request_id shows `mpt-7b-emb-v2.1` it routed to v2.1.
customer-ops: Ok, please pin us. Org id: `org_54321`. Also it's a bit rough that there wasn't an automatic warning — our ingestion started failing immediately. Any way to get alerts if vector_size changes for pinned or used models?
ryan-sre: Good feedback. We don't currently surface an explicit alert when `vector_size` changes for a model you have traffic to. I'll propose an SRE rule: when `model_id` used by an org changes `vector_size` between releases, emit a warning to the org owners and to support. I can file that. :memo:
mike-eng: For a quick mitigation script if you want to attempt temporary down-projection (not ideal): you can run an online PCA transform to reduce 1536->1024, but it will reduce quality. Example using sklearn:
```
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
pca = PCA(n_components=1024)
pca.fit(older_doc_embeddings)  # use a subset of your existing 1024 vectors
new_vec = pca.transform(new_1536_vec.reshape(1,-1))
```
We only recommend re-indexing as the long-term fix.
elllen-support: I've created a support ticket and queued a platform-level pin for `org_54321` to `mpt-7b-emb-v1.9`. ETA ~30m to complete and we'll confirm here when done. Also opened a billing/help note — if you want credits for the outage, please include an estimate of customer impact in the ticket.
customer-ops: Thanks — we can wait for the pin. We'll also schedule a re-index job. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :pray:
deply-bot: promoted mpt-7b-emb-v2.1 -> stable by release-engineering at 2024-11-02T22:14Z (canary run succeeded)
ryan-sre: Pin is in progress. After pin we recommend running a single test ingest to confirm FAISS accepts the dimension. If anything still fails paste request_id and we'll grab the logs.
customer-ops: Pin confirmed — test ingest now returns 1024 vectors. Our indexer accepted the batch. Thanks everyone, will follow up in the ticket for billing credits.
elllen-support: Closing the immediate loop here — follow-up tasks: 1) re-index to 1536 if you want to upgrade later, 2) confirm org-level pinning docs are updated (we'll add a note), 3) SRE to propose alerting rule. Assigning `support-12345`. If you need us to perform the re-index on your behalf let us know. :white_check_mark:
customer-ops: Great, closing from our side too. Thanks!
